The CAC registration fee for a business name is **₦10,000** [1]. This includes certified true copies of your registration documents.

Before you register, you'll also need to reserve your business name, which costs ₦500 per name [1]. The name reservation is valid for 60 days, so you need to complete the registration within that time.

The whole process usually takes 24 working hours once you've submitted everything online through the CAC's Company Registration Portal [1].

Please confirm these fees with CAC before paying, as they can change. You can check the latest on cac.gov.ng.

**Sources**

For NAFDAC product registration of your drink, you'll need to submit these documents [1]:

- **Application letter** for product registration, on your company letterhead, addressed to the Director-General (attention: the Director, Food Registration and Regulatory Affairs Directorate)
- **Evidence of business incorporation** (your CAC registration)
- **Batch formulation** (if applicable)
- **Evidence of payment** of the registration fee
- **Contract manufacturing agreement** (if you use a contract manufacturer)
- **Evidence of brand name registration** with the Trademarks Registry (Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment), in your name
- **Product labels or coloured artwork** showing the front, back, whole and side views
- **Comprehensive certificates of analysis** for your product

The registration fee depends on your business size: micro enterprise ₦22,000; small ₦30,000; medium/large ₦40,000 [1]. Processing takes about 180 working days from submission to approval [1]. **Confirm these fees with NAFDAC before paying, as the tariff information is from 2019.**

One important thing: NAFDAC won't accept your product registration application until your facility has passed inspection and your product has passed laboratory analysis [1]. The citation is excellent: every fact is marked with [1] and the source properly identifies both the document ("Opening a retail (community) pharmacy — Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN) requirements") and the specific section ("Premises meet PCN siting and structure standards"), matching the gold material exactly.

replies:
The PCN has strict rules about where your pharmacy can be located and how the building must be set up [1].

**Where you can site your pharmacy:**

Your pharmacy cannot be in a motor park, petrol station, market, clustered environment, kiosk, container or stall [1]. If you're opening a standalone pharmacy, it must be at least 200 metres from another standalone pharmacy, and also at least 200 metres from any pharmacy in a shopping centre [1]. If you're in a shopping centre, there can be no more than three pharmacies there, they cannot be next door to each other, and there must be at least five other shops between them [1]. Patent medicine shops must be at least 400 metres away [1]. Distances are measured from front main door to front main door by the shortest accessible route [1].

One important thing: if the area around your premises later becomes clustered or a market grows up around it, you'll have to relocate within two years [1].

**Your building must meet these standards:**

Minimum floor area of 30 square metres, with concrete walls, concrete or tiled floors, and a ceiling at least 3.05 metres high [1]. You'll need separate areas for dispensing, counselling, patient care, client waiting, and storage, plus an office for your superintendent pharmacist [1]. The premises must have good lighting and ventilation, with functional air conditioning and fans [1]. You'll also need fire extinguishers, a sand bucket, emergency exits, and must keep the premises and surroundings neat [1].

Before you apply for location approval, make sure your site meets these rules—PCN will inspect it against these standards [1].

**Sources**

1. Opening a retail (community) pharmacy — Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN) requirements — Premises meet PCN siting and structure standards (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [pcn.gov.ng](https://pcn.gov.ng/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Guidelines_for_Registration_of_Pharmacists_and_Pharmaceutical_Premises.pdf)

Your privacy notice must include these key pieces of information [1]:

- **Your business's name** and the lawful basis for processing personal data
- **What personal data you collect**, why you collect it, and how you use it
- **Who else has access to the data** and why (for example, payment processors, email services, or shipping partners)
- **Your customers' rights** over their data (like the right to access, correct or delete their information)
- **A contact person within your business** for complaints about how you handle their data
- **The customer's right to complain to NDPC**, the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, if they're not satisfied

The notice must be published on your website's homepage, and it's separate from your cookie banner. Remember that simply showing customers this information is not the same as getting their consent—you'll need to handle consent separately, especially for non-essential cookies [1].

One important note: your privacy notice must name your business, so you'll need to complete your CAC business registration first [1].

Here's your checklist for starting your zobo business in Ibadan. The steps follow the order the regulators require, and I've grouped them into stages so you can see what comes first.

## **Start here: Get your business legally registered**

1. **CAC business name registration** [1] — Register your business name with the Corporate Affairs Commission. You'll need two proposed names, your NIN or other ID, a passport photo, and your signature. The name search takes about 4 working hours, and registration takes 24 working hours. Cost: ₦500 per name reservation, plus ₦10,000 for registration.

2. **Federal Tax ID** [2] — Once your CAC registration is done, retrieve your Tax ID using your NIN on the NRS Tax ID portal. This is free and you'll need it for NAFDAC.

3. **Oyo State tax clearance** [3] — Get a personal income tax clearance certificate from Oyo State. You'll need this for your premises registration later.

## **Before you can make and sell zobo: NAFDAC facility and product approval**

4. **Set up your production facility to meet NAFDAC standards** [4] — Your facility needs at least one dedicated room with its own entrance and exit, pest control (screens and self-closing doors), good ventilation, a hand-washing station, proper waste disposal, and fumigation every three months. You'll also need food-grade equipment and records of where your raw materials come from so you can recall products if needed.

5. **Get food handler medical certificates** [5] — Anyone working in production must have a medical test certificate.

6. **Trademark registration** [6] — Register your zobo brand name with the Trademarks Registry. NAFDAC requires evidence of this before they'll inspect your facility. Cost: around ₦11,530 (confirm the exact fee).

7. **NAFDAC facility inspection application** [5] — Apply to NAFDAC with your CAC certificate, trademark registration, facility details, staff qualifications, production procedures, and the medical certificates. You'll propose an inspection date. NAFDAC will inspect your facility and either approve it or give you compliance directives to fix.

8. **Laboratory analysis of your zobo** [5] — Once your facility passes inspection, send samples of your zobo to a laboratory for analysis to confirm it meets NAFDAC's Fruit Juice and Nectar Regulations. (Note: zobo is not specifically named in the regulations, so confirm with NAFDAC how it's classified.)

9. **NAFDAC product registration** [5] — Submit your product registration application with the lab results, batch formulation, product labels, and all the documents from step 7. NAFDAC will review everything and take it to their approval meeting. Processing takes around 180 working days (confirm this with NAFDAC, as their guideline has conflicting dates). Cost: ₦22,000 for a micro enterprise.

## **Before you open: State and local permits**

10. **Oyo State business premises registration** [3] — Register your production premises with the Oyo State Ministry of Trade, Industry, Investment and Cooperatives. You'll need your CAC certificate and the tax clearance from step 3. The fee depends on your business category (confirm with the Ministry whether you fall under "manufacturing, small scale" or another category). You must renew this every year.

## **Once you're selling**

11. **Annual CAC returns** [1] — File your annual return with CAC each year. Cost: ₦3,000.

12. **Annual Oyo State premises renewal** [3] — Renew your state premises registration every year.

---

**Important notes:** NAFDAC's current guidelines say beverages are exempt from the simpler micro-scale category, which means you may need to meet the standard facility requirements (four rooms, fenced factory, treated water, full manufacturing practice) instead. **Confirm with NAFDAC whether your zobo qualifies for micro-scale listing or if you need standard facility approval.** Also, the fees and timelines I've quoted are from documents dated October 2026, so confirm them with each regulator before paying.

**Sources**

1. Business registration with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) — Business name registration — sole proprietorship (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [cac.gov.ng](https://www.cac.gov.ng/services/business-name)
2. Tax registration — federal (Nigeria Revenue Service) and state internal revenue services — Federal Tax ID (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [nrs.gov.ng](https://www.nrs.gov.ng/)
3. State business premises permits — Oyo, Lagos, FCT, Rivers, Ogun and Edo — Oyo State business premises registration (information as of 25 Oct 2026) · [trade.oyostate.gov.ng](https://trade.oyostate.gov.ng/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/PROCEDURES-FOR-REGISTRATION-OF-BUSINESS-PREMISES.pdf)
4. NAFDAC requirements for packaged fruit drinks made in Nigeria — Production facility meets NAFDAC requirements (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [nafdac.gov.ng](https://nafdac.gov.ng/food/guideline-for-micro-scale-enterprises/)
5. NAFDAC requirements for packaged fruit drinks made in Nigeria — NAFDAC facility inspection application and inspection (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [nafdac.gov.ng](https://nafdac.gov.ng/food/guideline-for-micro-scale-enterprises/)
6. Trademark registration — Trademarks, Patents and Designs Registry (Nigerian Intellectual Property Office) — Summary (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [nipo.gov.ng](https://nipo.gov.ng/trademark.jsp)

Here's the full checklist for opening your pharmacy in Lagos, in the order the regulators require:

**Start here**

1. **CAC business name registration** [1] — Register your partnership with the Corporate Affairs Commission. You'll need both partners' details, two proposed business names, and your business address. The name search takes about 4 working hours, and registration takes 24 working hours. Cost: ₦500 per name search plus ₦10,000 for registration. [1]

2. **Ensure you have a superintendent pharmacist** — Before you can apply to PCN, you need a registered pharmacist with a current annual licence to practise. This is a legal requirement. [2]

3. **Get PCN location approval** [3] — Apply to the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN) at their Lagos zonal or state office with your superintendent pharmacist's licence, your CAC certificate, and a signed disclaimer of liability form. PCN checks that your proposed site meets their siting requirements. This takes about two weeks. [3]

4. **Set up your premises to PCN standards** — While waiting for location approval, prepare your pharmacy building and equipment to meet PCN requirements. [2]

5. **Get PCN premises registration** [4] — Once your location is approved and your premises is ready, submit Form B (from the PCN office) with your superintendent pharmacist's licence, CAC certificate, and other documents. PCN will inspect the premises within one month. After inspection and approval, the PCN Registry issues your premises licence within 21 working days. [4]

**Once your PCN registration comes through**

6. **Federal tax registration (Tax ID)** — Register with the Nigeria Revenue Service to get your business Tax ID. You'll need your CAC certificate. [5]

7. **Lagos State tax registration** — Register on the LIRS eTax portal (etax.lirs.net) as a corporate taxpayer using your CAC number. [6]

8. **Lagos State business premises registration** — On the same LIRS eTax portal, register your premises and pay the registration fee. For an urban area in Lagos, this is up to ₦10,000; for a rural area, ₦2,000. [7]

**Before you open**

9. **Display your certificates and meet operating standards** — Once registered, display your PCN premises certificate and your superintendent pharmacist's licence visibly in the pharmacy. Keep a poisons book for controlled substances, and ensure only licensed pharmacists handle them. [2]

10. **Annual PCN premises renewal** — From 1 January each year, renew your PCN premises registration before 31 January. [2]

The PCN fees for location approval and premises registration could not be read clearly from their official form, so confirm those with the PCN Lagos office before paying. All other fees and timelines are current as of October 2026; confirm them with each regulator before you pay, as they can change.

## Your cosmetics import business checklist

Here's everything you need to do, in the right order. The steps follow the regulators' own rules, so some must be done before others.

### **Start here**

**1. CAC business registration (private company) [1]**
You need to register your company with the Corporate Affairs Commission first — it's the foundation for everything else. As a private company, you'll need to provide your company name, registered office address, directors' and shareholders' details, share capital (minimum ₦100,000), and a Memorandum and Articles of Association. Registration takes 24 working hours and costs ₦10,000 plus stamp duty (amount not stated in the official fee summary — confirm with CAC). [1]

**2. Trademark registration for your brand [2]**
NAFDAC requires evidence that your brand name is registered with the Trademarks Registry before you can register your products. File your application in Class 3 (cosmetics). You'll need a clear image of your mark (JPEG, at least 1200 dpi), your company details and a power of attorney if you use an agent. [2]

### **Once CAC and trademark are done**

**3. Federal Tax ID [3]**
Register on REV360 (selfservice.nrs.gov.ng) using your CAC registration number. The system checks your details against CAC records. There's no fee stated, but confirm with the Nigeria Revenue Service. [3]

**4. Lagos State tax registration [4]**
Register on the LIRS eTax portal (etax.lirs.net) as a corporate taxpayer using your CAC number. This is separate from federal tax. [4]

**5. Lagos State business premises registration [5]**
Also on the LIRS eTax portal, register your business premises. The fee is up to ₦10,000 for an urban area or ₦2,000 for a rural area, depending on where the LIRS classifies your location. [5]

### **Before you import and register your products**

**6. Check if your products are prohibited [6]**
NAFDAC maintains a list of cosmetics that cannot be imported. Confirm your products are not on it before you proceed.

**7. NAFDAC imported cosmetics registration application [7]**
Submit your application to NAFDAC's registration portal (registration.nafdac.gov.ng). You'll need your CAC certificate, trademark registration evidence, a notarised declaration, a power of attorney from your foreign manufacturer, a contract manufacturing agreement (both notarised in the country of manufacture), a Certificate of Manufacture and Free Sale (authenticated by the Nigerian Embassy or High Commission), product labels, a GMP inspection invitation letter from the manufacturer, and a certificate of analysis. [7]

**8. Electronic import permit and laboratory analysis [8]**
Once NAFDAC approves your application documents, they'll issue an electronic import permit. You can then bring in your products and submit samples for laboratory testing. [8]

**9. NAFDAC registration approval and certificate [9]**
Your product goes to NAFDAC's Food and Drug Registration Committee for final approval. This takes 120 working days from acceptance of your submission (the clock stops while NAFDAC queries are outstanding). Once approved, you receive an electronic Certificate of Product Registration, valid for five years. [9]

### **Data protection (if you handle more than 200 customers' data in six months)**

**10. Check if you're of major importance for data protection [10]**
If you collect customer names, phone numbers, addresses and payment details, and you'll have more than 200 customers within six months, you must register with the Nigeria Data Protection Commission. [10]

**11. Appoint a Data Protection Officer [11]**
If you're of major importance, designate a DPO (can be an employee or contractor) and send their contact details to NDPC. [11]

**12. Data protection impact assessment [12]**
Complete a DPIA for your online store before it goes live, have it vetted by your DPO, and file it with NDPC. [12]

**13. Register with NDPC [13]**
Register as an Ordinary High Level data controller. The fee is ₦10,000, and you must renew every year. [13]

### **Before you sell**

**14. Set up data protection policies [14]**
Create a privacy notice, a data protection policy, a privacy checklist, and data processing agreements with any third parties (payment providers, delivery, hosting). Train your staff within six months of starting. [14]

**15. VAT registration (if your turnover will exceed ₦100 million annually) [15]**
If you expect annual turnover above ₦100 million, register for VAT on REV360. Businesses with turnover of ₦100 million or less are exempt. [15]

---

The same applies to stamp duty for your CAC registration. Both registration guidelines are due for review on 12 December 2026, so confirm the current requirements with NAFDAC. Data protection fees and deadlines were updated in 2024–2025; check ndpc.gov.ng for any recent changes.

As a private company, you'll need to provide your company name, registered office address, directors' and shareholders' details, share capital (minimum ₦100,000), and a Memorandum and Articles of Association. Registration takes 24 working hours and costs ₦10,000 plus stamp duty (amount not stated in the official fee summary — confirm with CAC). [1]

**2. Trademark registration for your brand [2]**
NAFDAC requires evidence that your brand name is registered with the Trademarks Registry before you can register your products. File your application in Class 3 (cosmetics). You'll need a clear image of your mark (JPEG, at least 1200 dpi), your company details and a power of attorney if you use an agent. [2]

### **Once CAC and trademark are done**

**3. Federal Tax ID [3]**
Register on REV360 (selfservice.nrs.gov.ng) using your CAC registration number. The system checks your details against CAC records. There's no fee stated, but confirm with the Nigeria Revenue Service. [3]

**4. Lagos State tax registration [4]**
Register on the LIRS eTax portal (etax.lirs.net) as a corporate taxpayer using your CAC number. This is separate from federal tax. [4]

**5. Lagos State business premises registration [5]**
Also on the LIRS eTax portal, register your business premises. The fee is up to ₦10,000 for an urban area or ₦2,000 for a rural area, depending on where the LIRS classifies your location. [5]

### **Before you import and register your products**

**6. Check if your products are prohibited [6]**
NAFDAC maintains a list of cosmetics that cannot be imported. Confirm your products are not on it before you proceed.

**7. NAFDAC imported cosmetics registration application [7]**
Submit your application to NAFDAC's registration portal (registration.nafdac.gov.ng). You'll need your CAC certificate, trademark registration evidence, a notarised declaration, a power of attorney from your foreign manufacturer, a contract manufacturing agreement (both notarised in the country of manufacture), a Certificate of Manufacture and Free Sale (authenticated by the Nigerian Embassy or High Commission), product labels, a GMP inspection invitation letter from the manufacturer, and a certificate of analysis. [7]

**8. Electronic import permit and laboratory analysis [8]**
Once NAFDAC approves your application documents, they'll issue an electronic import permit. You can then bring in your products and submit samples for laboratory testing. [8]

**9. NAFDAC registration approval and certificate [9]**
Your product goes to NAFDAC's Food and Drug Registration Committee for final approval. This takes 120 working days from acceptance of your submission (the clock stops while NAFDAC queries are outstanding). Once approved, you receive an electronic Certificate of Product Registration, valid for five years. [9]

### **Data protection (if you handle more than 200 customers' data in six months)**

**10. Check if you're of major importance for data protection [10]**
If you collect customer names, phone numbers, addresses and payment details, and you'll have more than 200 customers within six months, you must register with the Nigeria Data Protection Commission. [10]

**11. Appoint a Data Protection Officer [11]**
If you're of major importance, designate a DPO (can be an employee or contractor) and send their contact details to NDPC. [11]

**12. Data protection impact assessment [12]**
Complete a DPIA for your online store before it goes live, have it vetted by your DPO, and file it with NDPC. [12]

**13. Register with NDPC [13]**
Register as an Ordinary High Level data controller. The fee is ₦10,000, and you must renew every year. [13]

### **Before you sell**

**14. Set up data protection policies [14]**
Create a privacy notice, a data protection policy, a privacy checklist, and data processing agreements with any third parties (payment providers, delivery, hosting). Train your staff within six months of starting. [14]

**15. VAT registration (if your turnover will exceed ₦100 million annually) [15]**
If you expect annual turnover above ₦100 million, register for VAT on REV360. Businesses with turnover of ₦100 million or less are exempt. [15]

---

**A few things to confirm before you start:** NAFDAC's fees for imported cosmetics registration and approval are set in their tariff but not shown in the public guidelines — ask them directly. The same applies to stamp duty for your CAC registration. Both registration guidelines are due for review on 12 December 2026, so confirm the current requirements with NAFDAC. Data protection fees and deadlines were updated in 2024–2025; check ndpc.gov.ng for any recent changes.

Personal data may only be processed on one of six lawful bases: consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interest, public interest or legitimate interest. Relying on legitimate interest needs a written Legitimate Interest Assessment. (Article 26(2)(a))

- Direct marketing, such as promotional emails, SMS or WhatsApp messages
- Sensitive personal data
- Using data for a new purpose that does not fit the original one
- Children's data
- Sending data to a country without an NDPC adequacy decision
- Fully automated decisions with significant effects on the person

- Keep records of consent.

- Give a clear accept or decline option for every consent request.

Here's your step-by-step checklist to run your furniture workshop legally in Ogun State. The steps follow the order the regulators require, and I've grouped them into stages so you can see what comes first.

## Start here: Federal registration

**1. CAC business name registration [1]**
Reserve and register your business name with the Corporate Affairs Commission. You'll need two proposed names, your NIN or other valid ID, a passport photo, and your business address. The name reservation costs ₦500 per name, and registration costs ₦10,000. It takes about 24 working hours once you've paid. You'll get an electronic Certificate of Registration—keep this safe, as you'll need it for the next steps.

**2. Federal Tax ID [2]**
Once your CAC registration comes through, retrieve your Tax ID using your NIN on the NRS Tax ID portal. This is a 13-digit number that replaces the old TIN. You'll need it for any other registrations and to open a business bank account.

## Before you open: State registration

**3. Ogun State business premises permit [3]**
Register your workshop premises online at https://businesspermit.ogunstate.gov.ng. Create a free account, register your business, generate the invoice, and pay online. The certificate is issued immediately. The fee is calculated by the portal and varies by business type and size—confirm the exact amount when you register. Once you have the certificate, **display it in a visible place at your workshop** for government inspection.

## Every year

**4. CAC annual returns [1]**
File your annual return with CAC each year. The fee is ₦3,000 for a sole proprietorship.

---

**A few notes:** If your business grows and your annual turnover goes above ₦100 million, you'll also need to register for VAT [2]. For now, as a small business, you're exempt. If you later hire employees, you'll also need to register for PAYE (pay-as-you-earn) tax with Ogun State.

The fees and timelines I've given are current as of late October 2026, but confirm them with CAC and the Ogun State Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment before paying, as they can change.

**Sources**

You can find their requirements at [ndpc.gov.ng](https://ndpc.gov.ng/dpco-registration-requirements/).

For your zobo drink business, here's what comes first:

**Start here:**

1. **CAC business registration** — Register your business name or company with the Corporate Affairs Commission. This is your foundation; NAFDAC won't process your product registration without proof of it.

2. **Facility inspection by NAFDAC** — Before NAFDAC will register your product, they need to inspect where you make the zobo to check it meets good manufacturing practice (GMP) standards. You'll need to apply for this inspection.

3. **Laboratory analysis** — Your zobo must be tested by an approved lab to confirm it meets NAFDAC's standards for fruit drinks. This report goes to NAFDAC with your product registration.

4. **NAFDAC product registration** — Once the inspection is satisfactory and the lab report is in, you submit your product registration application [1]. This takes about 180 working days to process [1]. The fee for a micro enterprise is ₦22,000 [1], though you should confirm the current fee with NAFDAC since tariffs can change.

5. **Product labelling** — After NAFDAC approves your product, you'll get a registration number that must appear on your label [1].

**Meanwhile:**

- **Trademark registration** — If you have a brand name for your zobo, register it with the Trademarks Registry (part of the Nigerian Intellectual Property Office) so NAFDAC knows you own it [1].
- **Tax registration** — Get your Tax ID (TIN) from the Nigeria Revenue Service and register for VAT with your state's internal revenue service.
- **State business premises permit** — In Oyo State, you'll need a permit for your production premises.
- **Data protection registration** — Register with the NDPC since you're keeping customer phone numbers.

The order matters because NAFDAC won't move forward without the inspection and lab results, and you can't sell until the product is registered. Would you like me to walk through any of these steps in more detail?

**Sources**

1. NAFDAC requirements for packaged fruit drinks made in Nigeria — NAFDAC product registration (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [nafdac.gov.ng](https://nafdac.gov.ng/food/guideline-for-micro-scale-enterprises/)

comparison.rationale: The answer includes several required steps but has significant ordering errors and omissions. It incorrectly states trademark registration must come before NAFDAC facility inspection (gold shows no such dependency), and places "Product composition meets the Fruit Juice and Nectar Regulations" nowhere despite it being required and having no prerequisites. Missing required steps include the trademark availability search (which must precede filing), examination and acceptance, and publication/opposition period. The answer also invents the claim that trademark registration is needed before NAFDAC inspection. Citations are vague—marking facts with [1] but listing three different sources without clear mapping, making verification difficult. The ordering violation (trademark before facility inspection when they're independent) and incomplete coverage warrant correctness=1.

You're at the point where you need to move into NAFDAC product registration. Before that, though, there are two steps in between that the documents show you'll need:

**Laboratory analysis of your product** comes first. NAFDAC won't register your drink until they've seen a comprehensive certificate of analysis showing your product meets the Fruit Juice and Nectar Regulations. You'll need to send samples to an accredited lab to get this done.

**Then NAFDAC product registration** [1]. This is where you formally register each product you make. You'll send an application letter, complete an online form at https://registration.nafdac.gov.ng, and submit documents including your product labels, the lab analysis certificate, and evidence of trademark registration. NAFDAC processes these over about 180 working days, and once approved, you'll get a registration number that must go on your label [1].

The registration fee depends on your business size. Since you're a sole proprietor making drinks locally, you'll likely fall into the micro or small enterprise category—that's ₦22,000 to ₦30,000 [1]. **Confirm the exact fee with NAFDAC before you pay**, because the tariff information is from 2019 and may have changed.

One important note: NAFDAC's guidelines say beverages are on an exempted list for micro-scale producers, but the documents disagree on whether that applies to you. **Check with NAFDAC directly** to confirm whether your setup qualifies for micro-scale registration or whether you need to meet the standard facility requirements.

You have two main steps left before you can open:

**1. Location approval from PCN [1]**  
PCN needs to approve the exact site where your pharmacy will be. You'll apply at the PCN Lagos state office with your superintendent pharmacist's current licence, your CAC partnership certificate, and a few other documents. PCN usually approves within two weeks if everything is in order [1]. The fee is set by PCN but wasn't clearly readable in their form, so confirm it with the PCN state office when you apply.

**2. Premises registration after inspection [1]**  
Once PCN approves the location, they'll inspect the finished premises to make sure it meets their standards. After the inspection passes, you get your premises registration certificate. This is what allows you to legally operate [1].

After that, you'll need to renew your premises registration every year by 31 January [1].

The next step is to contact the PCN Lagos state office with your documents and apply for location approval. Do you have the superintendent pharmacist's current annual licence and your CAC partnership certificate ready?

**Sources**

Good—you've got the foundation in place. Since you're importing your own brand, here's what's left:

**Before you can sell:**

1. **Check that your products aren't on NAFDAC's prohibition list** [1] — this is a quick step that comes before you apply for registration.

2. **Register each product with NAFDAC** [1] — you'll need to submit an application with your CAC certificate, trademark registration, a notarised declaration, a contract manufacturing agreement from your foreign supplier, a certificate of manufacture and free sale from the country where they're made (authenticated by the Nigerian Embassy), product labels, and a certificate of analysis from a testing lab. You upload these to NAFDAC's portal.

3. **Get an electronic import permit and lab analysis** [1] — NAFDAC issues this once your application is received.

4. **GMP inspection of your supplier's factory** [1] — NAFDAC will inspect where your products are made to confirm they meet standards.

**Meanwhile, for data protection:**

5. **Register with the National Data Protection Bureau** — since you collect customer data online, you'll need to register and have a data protection notice on your website. I can walk you through the details if you need them.

**Every year:**

6. **File your company's annual return with CAC** and **pay your company income tax** — these keep your registration active.

The NAFDAC product registration is the main step ahead. Once you've got your supplier's documents ready, you can start that application. Would you like me to go through the NAFDAC documents you'll need to gather, or do you have questions about any of these steps?

Now I can see the path ahead. The next step is to **get your CAC certificate of incorporation** [1]. You've registered your business name as a sole proprietor, but MANCAP needs the formal CAC certificate before you can apply for product certification [1].

Here's what comes after that:

1. **Get your CAC certificate of incorporation** — This is the formal document from CAC that proves your business is registered. You'll need it for the MANCAP application [1].

2. **Apply for MANCAP certification** — Once you have your CAC certificate, contact the SON state office in Ogun to get the MANCAP application form. You'll need to provide your CAC certificate, an on-the-spot test report of your product, and proof of payment [1]. You can also apply online at https://mancap.son.gov.ng/ [1].

3. **Factory inspection and product testing** — SON will inspect your factory and test your product to make sure it meets the Nigerian Industrial Standard [1].

4. **Receive your MANCAP certificate** — If everything passes, SON will issue your certificate and a numbered MANCAP logo within 60 days of receiving your application [1]. The certificate is valid for three years, and SON will inspect your factory every quarter during that time [1].

One thing to confirm with the SON Ogun state office: they may ask for a CAC certificate of incorporation rather than just a business name registration. Check with them about whether your sole proprietorship registration is enough, or whether you need to upgrade to a formal company registration with CAC first.

What's your next move—do you have your CAC certificate yet, or do you need help with that?

All facts are properly supported by the gold material with [1] citations, and the Sources section correctly names the document and section (Opening a retail pharmacy — PCN requirements — Premises meet PCN siting and structure standards). The only minor addition is the advice to confirm with PCN Lagos, which is reasonable practical guidance not contradicted by the gold material.

replies:
The PCN has strict rules about where your pharmacy can be located and how the building must be set up [1].

**Where you can site the pharmacy:**

Your pharmacy cannot be in a motor park, petrol station, market, clustered environment, kiosk, container or stall [1]. If you're opening a standalone pharmacy, it must be at least 200 metres from another standalone pharmacy, and also at least 200 metres from any pharmacy in a shopping centre [1]. Distances are measured from front main door to front main door by the shortest accessible route [1].

If you're planning to locate in a shopping centre, there can be no more than three pharmacies in that centre, they cannot be next door to each other, and there must be at least five shops between them [1]. Patent medicine shops must be at least 400 metres away [1].

The area around your pharmacy must stay sanitary. If the surroundings later become clustered or a market grows around it, you'll have to relocate within two years [1].

**The building itself:**

Your premises must have a minimum floor area of 30 square metres, with concrete walls, concrete or tiled floors, and a ceiling at least 3.05 metres high [1]. You'll need separate areas for dispensing, counselling, patient care, client waiting and storage, plus a furnished office for your superintendent pharmacist [1]. The space must have good lighting and ventilation, with functional air conditioning and fans [1]. You'll also need fire extinguishers, a sand bucket and emergency exits, and the premises and surroundings must be kept neat [1].

These are the siting rules PCN checks before approving your location. Confirm all the specific requirements with your PCN state office in Lagos before you commit to a site, as they can advise on how these rules apply to your exact location.

**Sources**

1. Opening a retail (community) pharmacy — Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN) requirements — Premises meet PCN siting and structure standards (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [pcn.gov.ng](https://pcn.gov.ng/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Guidelines_for_Registration_of_Pharmacists_and_Pharmaceutical_Premises.pdf)

replies:
Your privacy notice must include these key elements [1]:

- **Your business's name and the lawful basis** for processing customers' personal data
- **What personal data you collect**, why you collect it, and how you use it
- **Who else has access to the data** and why (for example, payment processors or delivery partners)
- **Customers' rights over their data** — what they can ask you to do with their information
- **A contact person within your business** for complaints about privacy
- **The customer's right to complain to NDPC** — the Nigeria Data Protection Commission

The notice must be published on your website's homepage, alongside a cookie banner if you use cookies [1]. Remember that simply showing customers this information is not the same as getting their consent to process their data — that's a separate step [1].

For cookies specifically: if you use cookies that aren't strictly necessary (like analytics or marketing cookies), visitors must be able to accept or reject them with an explicit choice. The cookie banner itself must be prominent — it can't be a small banner at the bottom that people might miss [1].

Since you're collecting personal data from customers, you'll also need to complete a data protection impact assessment before your online store goes live, and file it with NDPC [1]. That's a separate requirement, and I can walk you through it if you'd like.

The information above is current as of 24 October 2026. Confirm the exact requirements with NDPC before publishing, as data protection rules can be updated.

**Sources**

To apply for SON MANCAP certification, you have two routes [1]:

**Standard route:**
1. Contact the nearest SON state office to enquire and request the application form.
2. Alternatively, apply online at https://mancap.son.gov.ng/

**What you'll need to submit [1]:**
- Your CAC certificate of incorporation (or business name certificate — confirm with SON whether they accept sole proprietorships or partnerships, as this isn't stated in their guidance)
- An on-the-spot test report from SON, or if that's not comprehensive enough, a laboratory report from SON or from a laboratory accredited by the Institute of Public Analysts of Nigeria (IPAN)
- Proof of payment for the application form and certification fees

**Timeline:** Once SON receives your application with all requirements met, you'll get your certificate and MANCAP logo within 60 days [1]. The certificate is valid for three years, and SON will inspect your factory every quarter during that time.

**Fees:** SON publishes its fees at each state office and on its MANCAP administrative charges document, but the amounts aren't shown in the public guidance. You'll need to confirm the exact fees with your nearest SON state office.

**Faster option for small businesses:** If you're just starting out, SON also offers MANCAP Fast Track, which is a six-month verification that checks your production and quality capability. It's designed to help MSMEs get going quickly while they work toward full certification [1].

Since you're in Ogun and making furniture locally, MANCAP will be part of your path. It comes after your CAC registration and factory inspection. Would you like me to show you the full checklist for your furniture business?

**Sources**
1. Product certification for locally made products — Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) MANCAP — MANCAP application (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [son.gov.ng](https://son.gov.ng/mancapservice/)

Here's your ordered checklist. The steps follow the regulators' own rules, so you'll need to do them in this order to avoid delays.

**Start here — before you register anything**

1. **Product composition meets the Fruit Juice and Nectar Regulations** [1] — Make sure your zobo recipe and ingredients comply with NAFDAC's standards. This is the foundation; NAFDAC won't move forward without it.

2. **CAC business registration** [2] — Register your business name with the Corporate Affairs Commission. This is your first official step and unlocks most of what comes next.

3. **Trademark availability search** [3] — Check that your zobo brand name isn't already taken. You do this before filing the trademark application.

4. **Food handler medical tests for production staff** [1] — Your team needs health certificates. You can arrange these anytime, but NAFDAC will ask for them during inspection.

**Once your CAC registration comes through**

5. **Production facility meets NAFDAC requirements** [1] — Your kitchen or production space must meet NAFDAC's hygiene and equipment standards. You'll need this before the inspection.

6. **Federal Tax ID** [2] — Get your TIN (tax ID number) from the Nigeria Revenue Service.

7. **Oyo State tax registration** [2] — Register with Oyo State's tax authority.

8. **Trademark application (filing)** [3] — File your trademark with the Intellectual Property Office.

9. **Oyo State business premises registration** [2] — Register your production location with Oyo State's Ministry of Trade, Industry, Investment and Cooperatives.

**Before you can sell**

10. **NAFDAC facility inspection application and inspection** [1] — NAFDAC inspects your facility to confirm it meets their standards. This must happen before product registration.

11. **Laboratory analysis of registration samples** [1] — NAFDAC tests your zobo samples in their lab to confirm it meets the Fruit Juice and Nectar Regulations.

12. **NAFDAC product registration** [1] — Once the lab confirms your product is safe, NAFDAC registers it. This is your licence to sell.

13. **Product labelling** [1] — Your bottles must carry the correct NAFDAC-approved labels.

14. **Trademark examination, publication and registration** [3] — The Intellectual Property Office examines your trademark, publishes it for objections, and issues your certificate.

**Ongoing**

You'll also need to renew your CAC registration, state premises permit, NAFDAC product registration and trademark every few years, and keep your staff's medical tests current.

Would you like me to walk through any of these steps in detail — for example, what documents you'll need, fees, or timelines?

**Sources**

1. NAFDAC requirements for packaged fruit drinks made in Nigeria (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [nafdac.gov.ng](https://nafdac.gov.ng/food/guideline-for-micro-scale-enterprises/)
2. Business registration with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [www.cac.gov.ng](https://www.cac.gov.ng/services/business-name)
3. Trademark registration — Trademarks, Patents and Designs Registry (Nigerian Intellectual Property Office) (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [nipo.gov.ng](https://nipo.gov.ng/trademark.jsp)

comparison.rationale: The answer provides proper citations with numbered footnotes and a detailed sources list. However, there are significant ordering and completeness issues. The answer incorrectly places "Superintendent pharmacist registered and licensed" as step 1 in a "Start here — before CAC registration" section, but according to the gold material, "Location approval" must come after this step, and Location approval itself comes after several other steps including "Business ownership meets PCN rules" (which requires CAC registration first). This creates a logical impossibility in the presented order. Additionally, several required steps are missing entirely: "Check whether the business is of major importance" (required to determine if conditional steps apply), "Appoint a Data Protection Officer" (conditional), "VAT registration" (conditional), and "Register with NDPC as data controller or processor of major importance" (conditional recurring). The optional trademark process steps (filing, examination, publication, registration certificate) are also omitted except for the search. While conditional and optional steps may be summarized, omitting the conditional NDPC registration and the check that determines it is a significant gap.

Here's your checklist in order. I've grouped them into stages so you can see what comes first and what depends on earlier steps.

**Start here — before CAC registration**

1. **Superintendent pharmacist registered and licensed** [1] — You need a qualified pharmacist on your team. This is a PCN requirement and doesn't depend on anything else, so you can start it now.

2. **Premises meet PCN siting and structure standards** [1] — Your pharmacy location must meet PCN rules on where it can be and how it's built. Check this now too.

**Your foundation — CAC registration**

3. **CAC business registration** [2] — Register your partnership with the Corporate Affairs Commission. This is the key step that unlocks most of the others.

4. **Trademark availability search** [3] — Optional, but recommended. Check if your pharmacy name is available to trademark before you go further.

**Once CAC registration is done**

5. **Publish privacy policy, privacy notice and cookie notice** [4] — Since you collect customer data (like prescription records), you need to publish these notices.

6. **Lawful basis and consent for using customer data** [4] — Set up how you'll get and use customer data legally.

7. **Data security and breach reporting** [4] — Put systems in place to protect customer data and report any breaches.

8. **Business ownership meets PCN rules** [1] — PCN checks that your partnership structure is allowed for a pharmacy.

9. **Federal Tax ID** [5] — Register with the Nigeria Revenue Service.

10. **Lagos State tax registration** [5] — Register with Lagos State's tax authority.

11. **Lagos State business premises registration** [5] — Register your premises with Lagos State.

**Before you can open**

12. **Location approval** [1] — PCN approves your specific location. This needs your premises to meet standards, your ownership to be approved, and your superintendent pharmacist to be in place.

13. **Premises registration (pre-registration inspection and Form B)** [1] — PCN inspects your premises and registers them officially.

14. **Display certificates and meet operating standards** [1] — You'll display your PCN certificates and meet all operating rules.

**Every year**

15. **CAC annual returns** [2], **Lagos State business premises renewal** [5], **Annual renewal of premises registration** [1] — These repeat yearly to keep your pharmacy licensed.

The order follows the regulators' own rules: you need your superintendent pharmacist and premises ready first, then CAC registration unlocks the tax and data protection steps, and finally PCN approves your location and premises before you can open.

Here's your complete checklist in the right order. The steps follow the regulators' own rules—some things must come before others because one agency won't process you until another has approved you first.

**Start here (you can do these now)**

1. Confirm product not on import prohibition list [1] — NAFDAC won't register cosmetics that are banned, so check first.
2. CAC business registration [2] — Register your company with the Corporate Affairs Commission. This is your foundation; most other registrations wait for it.
3. Trademark availability search [3] — Search to make sure your brand name isn't already registered by someone else.
4. Confirm product needs MANCAP and its Nigerian Industrial Standard [4] — Check whether your cosmetics fall under SON's certification scheme. This is optional but recommended.

**Once your CAC registration comes through**

5. Check whether the business is of major importance [5] — The NDPC needs to know this to decide what data protection steps you'll need.
6. Publish privacy policy, privacy notice and cookie notice [5] — You collect customer data online, so you must publish these notices.
7. Lawful basis and consent for using customer data [5] — Set up how you'll get and use customer data legally.
8. Data security and breach reporting [5] — Put systems in place to protect customer data and report breaches if they happen.
9. Federal Tax ID [6] — Register with the Nigeria Revenue Service.
10. Lagos State tax registration [6] — Register with Lagos State Internal Revenue Service.
11. Trademark application (filing) [3] — File your trademark application once the search is clear.

**Before you can import and sell**

12. Examination and acceptance [3] — The trademark office examines your application.
13. Publication and opposition period [3] — Your trademark is published; others have time to object.
14. Registration certificate [3] — Once opposition ends, you get your trademark certificate.
15. Imported cosmetics registration application [1] — Now you can apply to NAFDAC to register your products.
16. Electronic import permit and laboratory analysis [1] — NAFDAC issues your import permit and arranges lab testing of your products.
17. GMP inspection of the foreign manufacturer [1] — NAFDAC inspects the factory where your cosmetics are made.
18. Registration approval and certificate [1] — Once the lab and factory checks pass, NAFDAC approves your products.

**Optional but recommended**

- MANCAP application [4] — If your products need SON certification, apply here.
- Lagos State business premises registration [7] — Register your business location with Lagos State.

**Every year**

- CAC annual returns [2]
- Company income tax and development levy [6]
- Trademark renewal [3] (every 10 years)
- Renewal of imported cosmetics registration [1]

Here's your step-by-step path to running your furniture workshop legally in Ogun State:

**Start here**

1. **CAC business registration** [1] — Register your business name as a sole proprietor with the Corporate Affairs Commission. This is your foundation; everything else depends on it.

2. **Confirm product needs MANCAP and its Nigerian Industrial Standard** [2] — Check with SON whether your furniture products need MANCAP certification (the mandatory conformity mark for locally made goods). This determines what comes next.

3. **Trademark availability search** [3] — Optional, but recommended. Search to make sure your business name or brand isn't already registered by someone else.

**Once your CAC registration comes through**

4. **Federal Tax ID** [4] — Register with the Nigeria Revenue Service to get your TIN (tax ID number).

5. **Ogun State tax registration** [4] — Register with Ogun State Internal Revenue Service (OGIRS).

6. **Ogun State Business Premises Permit** [5] — Get approval from Ogun State Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment for your workshop location.

**Before you can sell**

7. **MANCAP application** [2] — Once you have your CAC registration and know your products need MANCAP, apply to SON.

8. **Factory inspections and product conformity** [2] — SON will inspect your workshop and test your products to confirm they meet Nigerian standards.

9. **MANCAP certificate and logo** [2] — Once inspections pass, you'll receive your certificate and can use the MANCAP mark on your products.

**Ongoing**

10. **CAC annual returns** [1] — File every year to keep your registration active.

11. **Ogun State Business Premises Permit renewal** [5] — Renew as required by the state.

12. **MANCAP recertification** [2] — Recertify periodically to maintain your mark.

The trademark steps (search, filing, examination, publication, registration) are optional but recommended if you want to protect your brand name.

comparison.rationale: The answer provides proper citations with numbered footnotes and a detailed sources list. However, correctness is incomplete: it correctly excludes the already-completed CAC registration and covers most required steps, but has significant errors. Step 3 incorrectly describes "Food handler medical tests" as "a one-time requirement" when the gold marks it as recurring. More critically, the answer lists "Get your product labels approved by NAFDAC" (step 17) as a separate step requiring application, but the gold shows "Product labelling" as simply a requirement that comes after NAFDAC product registration, not a separate approval process. The grouping and ordering respect prerequisites correctly, and the answer appropriately summarizes recurring/optional steps in the "Ongoing requirements" section.

replies:
Here's what you need to do next, in order. I've grouped them into stages to make it clearer:

**Start here — before you set up your production**

1. Check that your product composition meets NAFDAC's Fruit Juice and Nectar Regulations [1]. This is the standard your drink must follow.
2. Search for your brand name at the Trademarks Registry to make sure no one else is using it [2].
3. Get medical tests done for anyone who will handle food in your production [1]. This is a one-time requirement, but you'll need to renew it regularly.
4. Make sure your production facility meets NAFDAC's requirements [1] — things like hygiene, equipment, and layout.

**Get your tax IDs and state permit**

5. Register for a Federal Tax ID with the Nigeria Revenue Service [4].
6. Register for tax with Oyo State Internal Revenue Service [4].
7. Register your business premises with Oyo State [5]. You'll need your state tax registration first.

**Trademark and optional product certification**

8. File your trademark application [2].
9. (Optional) Check if your product needs MANCAP certification from SON [3]. This is recommended but not required.
10. Wait for the trademark examination and acceptance [2].
11. (Optional) If you're doing MANCAP, apply for it [3].
12. Wait for the trademark publication and opposition period [2].
13. (Optional) If you're doing MANCAP, have SON inspect your factory and test your product [3].

**NAFDAC facility inspection and product registration**

14. Apply for NAFDAC facility inspection and have them inspect your production site [1]. You'll need your Federal Tax ID, your facility to be ready, and your food handlers' medical tests done.
15. Send samples to a lab for NAFDAC analysis [1].
16. Register your product with NAFDAC [1]. This is the key approval that lets you sell.
17. Get your product labels approved by NAFDAC [1].

**Ongoing requirements**

18. File CAC annual returns every year [6].
19. Renew your Oyo State business premises registration [5].
20. Renew your NAFDAC product registration [1].
21. Renew your trademark [2].

comparison.rationale: The answer covers several required steps but has significant issues: (1) Order violation: "Product composition meets regulations" is described as "the first step because everything else depends on it" and placed before NAFDAC facility inspection, but the gold shows it must come AFTER "NAFDAC facility inspection application and inspection" (Laboratory analysis requires both). (2) Missing critical step: NAFDAC facility inspection is mentioned only in passing ("NAFDAC will inspect your facility") but not listed as a distinct to-do step the user must initiate now. (3) VAT registration (conditional, can start now) is omitted entirely. (4) Citations are vague—markers point to entire documents rather than sections, and some facts lack markers (e.g., the Oyo premises registration claim has no citation at the point of use).

Great progress. You've got the foundation in place. Here's what comes next, in order:

**Ready to start now:**

1. **Product composition meets the Fruit Juice and Nectar Regulations** [1] — NAFDAC needs to confirm your drink formula complies with their standards before they'll register it. This is the first step because everything else depends on it.

2. **Trademark availability search** [2] — Check that your brand name isn't already registered. You need this before you can file for your own trademark.

3. **Oyo State tax registration** [4] — Register with the Oyo State tax authority. This is separate from your federal Tax ID and is required before you can register your business premises with the state.

**After those three:**

Once you've confirmed your product composition and done the state tax registration, you can apply for your **Oyo State business premises registration** [5]. This lets you legally operate your production facility in the state.

Meanwhile, after the trademark search comes back clear, you'll file your **trademark application** [2] with the national registry.

**Before you can sell:**

The big one is **NAFDAC product registration** [1]. NAFDAC will inspect your facility (you've already set it up), test samples of your drink in a lab, and then register the product. Only after that can you legally sell it. You'll also need to get your labels approved by NAFDAC [1].

**Optional but recommended:**

Check whether your drink needs **MANCAP certification** from SON (the standards body) [3]. It's not mandatory, but it can help with quality and customer trust.

It correctly excludes the already-completed steps (CAC, superintendent licensing, premises standards). The order respects all prerequisites: location approval comes before premises registration, which comes before displaying certificates; Federal Tax ID is mentioned before VAT (conditional). Optional steps like trademark registration are appropriately labeled. replies:
Good progress. You have several steps left before you can open, and then some recurring ones each year. Here's what comes next:

**Before you open:**

1. **Publish privacy notices** [2] — You collect customer data (prescription records, contact details), so you must publish a privacy policy and privacy notice explaining how you use it. This is required by law.

2. **Get lawful basis and consent** [2] — You need to document that customers have agreed to how you use their data, and that you have a legal reason to collect it.

3. **Set up data security and breach reporting** [2] — You must have a plan for keeping customer data safe and know how to report if there's a breach.

4. **Get your Federal Tax ID** [3] — Register with the Nigeria Revenue Service to get your TIN (tax ID number).

5. **Register with Lagos State tax** [3] — Register separately with the Lagos State Internal Revenue Service.

6. **Register your business premises with Lagos State** [4] — This is a state-level registration for your pharmacy location.

7. **Get PCN location approval** [5] — The Pharmacy Council must approve your specific location before you can proceed.

8. **PCN premises registration and inspection** [5] — Once location approval comes through, the PCN will inspect your premises and issue Form B.

9. **Display certificates and meet operating standards** [5] — After premises registration, you'll display your PCN certificate and ensure everything meets their standards.

**Optional but recommended:**

You can also search for trademark availability and register your pharmacy's name as a trademark, but this is not mandatory.

**Every year:**

Once you're open, you'll need to file CAC annual returns, renew your Lagos State premises registration, and renew your PCN premises registration.

comparison.rationale: The answer correctly excludes the completed steps and provides proper citations with numbered footnotes and a sources list. However, there are significant errors: (1) It incorrectly states "NAFDAC says your business is of major importance" when NDPC determines this; (2) It places "Trademark examination and acceptance" in a later stage when it can start now (the gold shows it has no prerequisites); (3) It lists "CAC annual returns" as ready to start now, which is correct, but then says "you can do this now, though it's due yearly" which is misleading since recurring tasks should be grouped separately; (4) The grouping creates an incorrect dependency structure suggesting trademark examination must wait. The order violation (examination and acceptance appearing after steps that can start now but presented as if it must wait) and the NAFDAC/NDPC confusion significantly impact correctness.

replies:
Here's what's left to do. I've grouped them into stages so you can see what comes first:

**Start now (ready to go)**

1. Confirm product not on import prohibition list [1] — NAFDAC needs to know your cosmetics aren't banned from import.
2. Check whether the business is of major importance [3] — This decides whether you need a Data Protection Officer and NDPC registration later.
3. Publish privacy policy, privacy notice and cookie notice [3] — Since you collect customer data online, you must publish these on your website.
4. Lawful basis and consent for using customer data [3] — You need to show you have a legal reason to use customer data and that customers have consented.
5. Data security and breach reporting [3] — Set up systems to protect customer data and a plan for reporting breaches.
6. Federal Tax ID [4] — Register with the Nigeria Revenue Service.
7. Lagos State tax registration [4] — Register with the Lagos State Internal Revenue Service.
8. CAC annual returns [7] — File your company's annual returns with CAC (you can do this now, though it's due yearly).

**Once your trademark examination is done**

9. Trademark examination and acceptance [6] — The registry reviews your application.
10. Publication and opposition period [6] — Your trademark is published; others can object for a set time.
11. Trademark registration certificate [6] — Once opposition ends, you get your certificate.

**Once you have your trademark certificate and NAFDAC clearance**

12. Imported cosmetics registration application [1] — Apply to NAFDAC to register your specific products.
13. Electronic import permit and laboratory analysis [1] — NAFDAC issues a permit and arranges lab testing.
14. GMP inspection of the foreign manufacturer [1] — NAFDAC inspects where your products are made.
15. Registration approval and certificate [1] — Once testing and inspection pass, NAFDAC approves your products.

**Conditional steps (only if needed)**

- If NAFDAC says your business is of major importance: appoint a Data Protection Officer, then do a data protection impact assessment.
- If your business grows beyond small-business size: register for VAT.
- If your cosmetics need a Nigerian Industrial Standard: apply for MANCAP certification (optional but recommended).

**Yearly tasks**

- File company income tax and development levy with the Nigeria Revenue Service.
- If you registered for MANCAP, renew it yearly.
- Renew your trademark every 10 years.
- Renew your NAFDAC cosmetics registration yearly.

comparison.rationale: The answer correctly identifies all required steps (Federal Tax ID, Ogun State tax registration, Business Premises Permit, MANCAP application, factory inspections, MANCAP certificate) and appropriately summarizes optional trademark steps and recurring obligations. It correctly does NOT list the two already-completed steps as to-dos, instead asking for confirmation. The order respects all prerequisites: steps that can start now are listed first, factory inspections come after MANCAP application, and certificate comes after inspections. All facts are supported by the cited sources, with proper footnotes linking to the correct documents and sections.

replies:
Here's what's left to do, in order:

**Start here (you can do these now)**

1. **Federal Tax ID** [2] — Register with the Nigeria Revenue Service. This is required before you can operate legally.

2. **Ogun State tax registration** [2] — Register with the Ogun State Internal Revenue Service. Your state also needs to know you're in business.

3. **Ogun State Business Premises Permit** [3] — Get approval from the Ogun State Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment for your production location. You'll need this before SON can inspect your factory.

4. **MANCAP application** [4] — Submit your application to the Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON). This is the formal step after confirming your product needs certification.

**Once MANCAP is approved**

5. **Factory inspections and product conformity** [4] — SON will inspect your facility and test your products to make sure they meet the Nigerian Industrial Standard.

6. **MANCAP certificate and logo** [4] — Once inspection passes, you'll get your certificate and can use the MANCAP mark on your products.

**Optional but recommended**

You can also do a trademark availability search [1] and file for trademark registration if you want to protect your brand name—this is optional for furniture but worth considering.

**Every year**

You'll need to file CAC annual returns [5] and renew your state premises permit and MANCAP certification when they expire.

Before I update your record, can you confirm that I should mark both your business name registration and the MANCAP confirmation as done?

**Sources**

1. Trademark registration — Trademarks, Patents and Designs Registry (Nigerian Intellectual Property Office) (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [nipo.gov.ng](https://nipo.gov.ng/trademark.jsp)
2. Tax registration — federal (Nigeria Revenue Service) and state internal revenue services (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [www.nrs.gov.ng](https://www.nrs.gov.ng/)
3. State business premises permits — Oyo, Lagos, FCT, Rivers, Ogun and Edo (information as of 25 Oct 2026) · [trade.oyostate.gov.ng](https://trade.oyostate.gov.ng/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/PROCEDURES-FOR-REGISTRATION-OF-BUSINESS-PREMISES.pdf)
4. Product certification for locally made products — Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) MANCAP (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [son.gov.ng](https://son.gov.ng/mancapservice/)
5. Business registration with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [www.cac.gov.ng](https://www.cac.gov.ng/services/business-name)
